# Project Agent Rules

Conventional baseline for AI coding agents working in this repository.

## Language

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in code, comments, or documentation.

## Code style

- Keep changes consistent with the surrounding code, its structure, naming, and patterns.
- Use `#region` to group related sections of code, never standalone separator lines.
- Write one property per line in object literals with two or more properties, including nested objects.
- Do not use alignment padding in assignments or comments.
- Avoid em-dash characters in code, comments, and user-facing text. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses.
- Use proper accents in all user-facing localized strings.
- Preserve existing code comments when editing. Do not delete or rewrite them during refactors.

## Robustness and safety

- Use typed domain error classes instead of generic errors for business logic.
- Never annotate catch variables as `any`; use `unknown`.
- Use `import type` at the top of the file instead of inline `import()` for types.
- Avoid unsafe type assertions such as `as any`. Prefer guards, augmentation, or validated data.
- Avoid global pollution. Use namespaces, classes, or object literals for helpers and registries.
- Design APIs and options for future extension without breaking existing call sites.
- Prefer atomic, cluster-safe operations because systems may run across multiple nodes with shared state.

## Directory and file organization

- One concept maps to one directory and one implementation. Avoid duplicates.
- Feature folders should contain only their own handler files.
- Test artifacts belong under `tests/`, never under `src/`.
- Respect recent user changes. Never revert or override user edits.
- Enforce a maximum file size; split overly large files into focused sub-modules.
- Extract repeated snippets found in three or more places into a shared utility.

## Testing

- When the repository already has a test runner configured, write tests for new behavior.
- Integration and end-to-end tests live under `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e`, with separate scripts, and cover complete user flows rather than single-button smoke checks.
- Treat lint warnings as errors and fix all diagnostics in files you edit.

## Commits

- Write commit messages in English by default and keep conventional-commit prefixes unchanged.
- Use the predominant language of the repository's history when that history is clearly non-English.

## Security note

- Operational credentials, secret values, token locations, and vault paths are intentionally omitted from this baseline.
- Consult the organization's dedicated secret-management documentation when handling credentials. Never print, commit, or embed secret values in source or documentation.
